stem: In her school laboratory, Meena observes two cells under a microscope during a biology practical in Pune. Cell P is thin and flat, forming a protective lining on the inside of the cheek. Cell Q is very long with thread-like branches and carries messages between the brain and the rest of the body. Which statement best explains how the shape and structure of each cell suit its function?

options.text: Cell P is thin and flat, which helps it form a protective layer, while Cell Q is long and branched, which helps it carry messages quickly over long distances.
Cell P is long and branched so it can carry messages, while Cell Q is thin and flat so it can form a protective lining.
Both cells have the same shape because they come from the same person's body, and their shape does not affect their function.
Cell Q is long because carrying messages stretches it out over time, while Cell P is flat because it has no specific function.

teacher.key_rationale: Flat thin cheek cells suit a protective lining function; elongated branched nerve cells suit message transmission over distances. A states this correct structure-function match. B reverses the relationship, C denies that shape matters, and D claims the shape is caused by stretching rather than being an adaptation.
